title: Harden settings schema persistence and backend policy ownership
summary: Implements verified settings schema/defaults/persistence review findings for defaulted network retry validation, duplicate-key strict JSON rejection, strict JSON-in-text config handling, backend-owned LibraryProfiles compatibility derivation, and explicit preserved-unknown-key preview/save evidence.
reason: The operator requested implementation of verified actionable findings from the settings schema/defaults/persistence and backend-vs-WebView policy ownership review. Settings persistence, strict JSON handling, library profiles, and backend policy ownership are high-validation boundaries.
behavior_before: Settings preview/save validation could reject configs missing defaulted CoordinatorMaxJobRetries, API JSON parsing rejected non-finite numbers but silently collapsed duplicate object keys, JSON-in-text config fields accepted non-finite and duplicate-key JSON, the Library Profiles WebView derived backend compatibility and promotion-rule keys, and preserved unknown config keys were retained without explicit preview/save evidence.
behavior_after: Settings validation materializes canonical Config defaults before numeric policy checks, API request/query parsing and config JSON-in-text parsing use duplicate-key and non-finite strict JSON handling, Library Profiles sends only LibraryProfiles and leaves mirrored compatibility/promotion keys to backend preview/save, and preview/save responses report preserved unknown config keys with warnings while still rejecting frontend attempts to mutate unknown keys.
